about: The weekly Torah reading as a way into this dataset. Most people find their place in the Torah by parashah rather than by chapter, so this file maps each of the fifty-four parashiyot to the literary units it touches, and each unit to the parashiyot it falls in.
source_of_the_parashah_divisions: The parashah boundaries are the standard ones, taken from Sefaria’s index of the Five Books. They are not a product of this research and have not been adjusted to fit it.
how_to_use: Find the parashah by name or number and read its units list. Each entry says whether that unit lies wholly inside the parashah or continues past it, and gives the verses the two have in common. by_unit does the reverse, naming the parashiyot each unit falls in.

relationship.note: The two divisions are independent of one another. They are not in conflict; they answer different questions. The parashiyot divide the Torah for reading aloud across a year; the units divide it by literary composition. Where they coincide is as informative as where they do not, and both are recorded here without adjustment.

languages: Parashah names are given in English and Hebrew; book names and verse ranges in English and in Hebrew numerals. Unit titles are in English only: the source edition names each unit by its book and number rather than by a title, so no Hebrew title exists to give.
